clue.text: Doctors go to Ecuador's capital-malaria risk

parts.note: MOs are medical officers, army doctors
Quito is the capital city of Ecuador

explanation.surface: Medics travelling to Quito are warned about the risk of malaria.
explanation.definitionFit: The insect carries the parasite that causes malaria, so it is the risk itself.

clue.text: Its prince chose gold at Belmont

definitions.text: Its prince chose gold at Belmont

parts.words: Its prince chose gold at Belmont
parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice, the North African suitor of Portia picks the golden casket at Belmont

explanation.surface: A royal suitor picks the gold option at a grand estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Portia lives at Belmont; her suitors choose among gold, silver and lead caskets.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's prince who chose the golden casket comes from this North African country.

clue.text: Put a new variety into roofing material, with a broad flat end

indicators.note: into signals that one piece goes inside the roofing material

parts.note: slate is used to tile roofs

indicators.note: a new variety of the letters means they are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Instructions to insert a new type into roof tiling with a wide, flat end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new variety' rearranges PUT A into PATU, which goes into SLATE after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped like a spatula, with a broad blunt end, is the botanical and anatomical meaning.

clue.text: Get hammock off hook (a sort of sun-fish)

indicators.note: a sort of the word means a reshuffled version of it

parts.note: ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Taking a hammock down, with a note about a kind of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges SUN into UNS, followed by LING.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhook a slung item such as a hammock is to take it down from where it hangs.

clue.text: Endless uproar over us making this barrow

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits on top of the next
endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a tumult is a noisy uproar
taken as written

explanation.surface: Constant noise about us building a wheelbarrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barrow' is not a wheelbarrow but an ancient burial mound.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is an ancient earth mound raised over a grave.

clue.text: Corporation has article in popular weekly

indicators.note: the word in tells us the article sits inside the magazine's name

parts.note: Punch was a famous British humorous weekly magazine
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A big company gets a piece written about it in a well-read weekly magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old jokey word for a large belly, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is dated slang for a pot belly, the same thing as a protruding stomach.

clue.text: What OT books do in order to provide past authority

definitions.meaning: Old Testament books come before NT, the New Testament
an earlier decision or case used as a guide or justification

explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'precede NT', it describes the Old Testament coming before the New; as one word it is an earlier ruling used as authority.

clue.text: Application by a French gentleman to import uranium

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the gentleman takes the uranium inside

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A French gentleman applies for permission to bring in uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Application' means an ointment applied to skin, not a request.
explanation.definitionFit: An ointment is something applied to the skin.

clue.text: He supplies King Charles with a new tree to hide inside

indicators.note: the king's initials hide the next piece inside them

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles

indicators.note: a new form of the letters is a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man brings King Charles a fresh tree to hide in, like the Royal Oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges A TREE into ATERE, held within C...R.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who provides food and drink for events is a supplier.

clue.text: See marbles scattered-what to do?

indicators.note: letters strewn about like dropped marbles are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has knocked over a bag of marbles and wonders what to do next.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the letters of SEE MARBLES rearranged, and what you must do with scattered marbles is gather them together again.
explanation.definitionFit: When marbles are scattered you must put them back together, collecting them into one group again.

clue.text: No Saul and Jonathan death report here, please

definitions.text: No Saul and Jonathan death report here, please

parts.words: No Saul and Jonathan death report here, please
parts.note: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan in 2 Samuel says 'Tell it not in' this Philistine city, lest the enemy rejoice

explanation.surface: A request that news of two biblical deaths not be announced in a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bible line 'Tell it not in Gath, publish it not in the streets of Askelon' (2 Samuel 1:20) is the key.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical lament asks that the news of the deaths be kept from this Philistine town.

clue.text: On the side of the head, a ring souvenir

definitions.text: On the side of the head, a ring souvenir

parts.words: On the side of the head, a ring souvenir
parts.note: a boxer leaves the boxing ring with a lasting memento: a swollen, misshapen ear

explanation.surface: A keepsake from a boxing match worn on the side of one's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' is the boxing ring, not jewellery: repeated blows deform a boxer's ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers often end up with a permanently swollen, lumpy ear from punches taken in the ring.

clue.text: Juicy fruit, but nothing to old style cookers

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing
kitchen ranges were old-fashioned solid-fuel cooking stoves

explanation.surface: A remark that citrus fruit has nothing on old-fashioned stoves.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus fruit such as these are notably juicy.

clue.text: Like Augustus refusing soup. Iced tea ma ordered

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Mother orders iced tea for a boy who refuses his soup.
explanation.walkthrough: In Struwwelpeter, Augustus refuses his soup, wastes away and dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Augustus grew thinner and thinner from not eating, becoming wasted and skeletal.

clue.text: Worn by the acrobat Pope, late of Paris

parts.note: Leo is the name of many popes
tard is French for late

explanation.surface: Something worn by a circus acrobat who used to live in Paris and is called Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight one-piece garment is what acrobats and dancers wear to perform.

clue.text: Arcadian fun'?

parts.note: the fun found in a games arcade, not in pastoral Arcadia

explanation.definitionFit: An arcade of slot machines is a place of entertainment and fun.

clue.text: Workers grow fat on furniture polish

parts.note: worker bees are the classic crossword workers
to wax is to grow larger, as the moon waxes

explanation.surface: Labourers put on weight while working with polish for furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Wax from the honeycomb is a traditional polish rubbed into wooden furniture.

clue.text: Back from Witchville, with directions

parts.note: the Witch of Endor appears in 1 Samuel, so Endor is the witch's town
S and E are compass directions

explanation.surface: Returning from a town of witches with instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' is the verb, to support, not a return.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or approve something is to back it.

clue.text: He has sting-anag. for 18 *" the sign"

annotationWithheld.why: He has sting-anag. for " the sign" (7): SCORPIO is the stinging sign, but 'anag. for' has no fodder that gives the answer, so the parse cannot be shown
annotationWithheld.clue: He has sting-anag. for 18 *" the sign"

clue.text: Spurs £2 ? Must be wrong

indicators.note: letters that must be wrong are put in a different order

parts.note: L is the pound sign's letter (libra) and II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone sees a price of two pounds for spurs and thinks it must be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: '£2' gives L for pounds plus II, the Roman two; mixed with MUST these make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spurs are things that urge on or provoke, which is what incentives are.

clue.text: Playful joke thus captures many a German heart

indicators.note: captures means the word for thus holds the other pieces

parts.note: so means thus
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
Herz is German for heart

explanation.surface: A light-hearted jest wins over many a German.
explanation.walkthrough: The file's clue was misread; the page prints this one. The musical term is Italian for 'joke'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is Italian for a jest and names a lively, playful movement in music.

clue.text: Set aside one note on tea-blending

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
sol is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: blending mixes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Putting aside a note about blending tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside is to separate or keep apart.

clue.text: Will gin diet maybe get us fired ?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a diet of gin might get us sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' means set alight, not dismissed as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set alight has been fired.

clue.text: Insignificant contribution made by the bathysphere?

definitions.text: Insignificant contribution made by the bathysphere?

parts.words: Insignificant contribution made by the bathysphere?
parts.note: a deep-sea diving sphere is literally lowered into the sea, which is also an idiom for a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A diving vessel's tiny part in some great enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: A bathysphere is a sphere lowered by cable for deep-sea observation, so it literally goes down into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an amount too small to matter compared with what is needed.

clue.text: Note the epitaph of Barnaby's raven

parts.note: G is a musical note
RIP, requiescat in pace, is the standard tombstone inscription

explanation.surface: A remark about the inscription on a raven's grave.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's novel Barnaby Rudge, Barnaby keeps a talking pet raven.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens named Barnaby Rudge's talking pet bird this.

clue.text: Our man's back in the marquee for the contest

indicators.note: the word in places the earlier pieces inside the big tent

parts.note: a marquee is a large tent
taken as written

indicators.note: back means the word man is read from right to left

parts.note: man, with the 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: Our representative has returned to the big tent where the competition is held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MAN into NAM; OUR plus NAM go inside TENT, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition of many matches between players is a contest.

clue.text: A short time back

definitions.meaning: a moment, a tiny unit of time
to back or support a motion or proposal

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a brief instant (one sixtieth of a minute) and a verb meaning to support a proposal.

clue.text: Underground workers Edward annoyed

parts.note: moles burrow and dig underground
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Miners pestered a man named Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pestered or harassed is to be bothered, an older sense of this word.
